declared: The fixture-evidenced Workshop surface reconstructed by deltin_rs::reconstruct (#125). The reconstructor converts validated WIR whose constructs lie on this surface into deterministic canonical OSTW that the native deltin-rs source implementation accepts; constructs outside the surface fail explicitly with structured diagnostics and no partial output.

rejected.reason: The per-player loop form has no OSTW source form on the declared surface (the frontend lowers loop counters as globals).
Custom-game settings (Program.settings) have no OSTW source form.
An action call whose catalog id has no OSTW source binding (e.g. createBeamEffect) cannot be emitted.
A value call whose catalog id has no OSTW source binding (e.g. getHealth) cannot be emitted.
An enum domain/member with no OSTW source binding cannot be emitted.
Raise To Power has no OSTW augmented-assignment form on the declared surface.
Remove From Array has no OSTW augmented-assignment form on the declared surface.
A rule condition that is not a two-operand comparison call would render as `value == True` in the shared Workshop emitter and cannot round-trip.

A bound call supplying fewer or more arguments than the canonical catalog arity would be re-resolved by the frontend with default filling or rejected; full canonical arity is required for a byte-stable round trip.
Variable/subroutine names colliding with builtin source names, enum domain source names, or each other (global vs player) would be shadowed by the frontend's resolution.
An empty variable/subroutine name is not a valid OSTW identifier.
A subroutine without its single non-empty, condition-free body rule cannot round-trip (the Workshop emitter drops empty-action rules).
A player-variable modify with a non-Event-Player receiver would lower back as a Set with a binary value, not a Modify.
A customString/format value whose text argument is not a string literal cannot be emitted as a `<"...">` format string.
A strict-greater comparison inside a reconstructed format string would terminate the OSTW `<"..."` string.
A number spelling outside the OSTW lexer's `[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?` form cannot round-trip.

notes: Variable-table identity (names, slots, player-vs-global placement) is outside the declared semantic comparison (the #119 normalization contract); the reconstructor emits `Any`-typed declarations and never recovers original types, indexes, comments, classes, macros, functions, or project structure. `Any` is the permissive universal OSTW type: the WIR carries no type information, and both the native frontend and the pinned v3.4.0 reference accept it.

Arithmetic values (catalog ids add/subtract/multiply/divide) are emitted as the real OSTW infix operators `+ - * /` (the reference rejects callable `Add(...)` forms); the shared Workshop emitter canonicalizes them back to the catalog spellings, so the round trip is byte-stable.

The reconstructed `.append(value)` form for the Workshop Modify-Append-To-Array action is accepted by the native deltin-rs source implementation (the declared acceptance bar) but the pinned v3.4.0 reference rejects member-call methods (documented divergence; recorded in the optional oracle cross-check under the reference-only contract).

The reverse binding table in src/signature.rs contains additional emittable catalog ids beyond the declared surface (e.g. skip, emptyArray, appendToArray, removeFromArray, currentArrayElement, currentArrayIndex, createEffect, modifyGlobalVariable, mappedArray, sortedArray); they are emittable through the same reverse bindings but are not fixture-evidenced on the reconstruction path and are not part of this declared surface.
Reconstructed OSTW always targets a single generated project root (ds.toml with entry_point plus main.ostw) inside the native frontend; no CLI/driver integration is added by #125.
The reconstruction fixtures and boundary are retained as owner-side evidence for the declared surface; the native reconstruction implementation has focused coverage in src/reconstruct.rs.
